articles.title: Intramedullary Bone Transport Nail for the Treatment of Segmental Tibial Bone Defect After Acute Traumatic Bone Loss.
articles.authors: Scolaro JA
articles.population: Young patient with open tibial shaft fracture
articles.outcomes: Successful reconstruction of 67 mm diaphyseal tibial defect
articles.take_home: An internal bone transport nail can successfully rebuild large gaps in the shinbone caused by traumatic injury. This method avoids the need for external pins and frames that stick out through the skin.

articles.title: Transport Intramedullary Nail for Nonunion.
articles.authors: Crist BD, Lee MA
articles.population: Patients with nonunion and bone defects
articles.outcomes: Bone healing, soft tissue complications, residual deformity, anatomical alignment
articles.take_home: Internal bone transport using an intramedullary nail is simpler for patients and avoids soft tissue problems associated with external devices while maintaining proper bone alignment. The review covers the key surgical techniques needed for this procedure.

articles.title: Advancements in Managing Bone Defects with Limb Length Discrepancies with a Motorized Intramedullary Combined Transport and Lengthening Nail.
articles.authors: Collins AC, Marecek GS
articles.population: Patients with large bone defects and limb length discrepancy requiring limb reconstruction
articles.outcomes: Technical feasibility and clinical outcomes of motorized intramedullary nails for combined bone transport and limb lengthening
articles.take_home: Motorized intramedullary nails that can perform both bone transport and lengthening in one implant represent an advance over previous methods that required multiple devices or staged procedures. The review examines how these newer nails work and when they may be beneficial for patients with bone defects and limb length differences.

articles.title: New Technology for the Treatment of Bone Defects and Limb Length Discrepancies with a Motorized Intramedullary Bone Transport Nail.
articles.authors: Frumberg DB, Vasudevan RS, Wellings EP
articles.population: Patients with bone defects and limb length discrepancies
articles.outcomes: Fully implantable motorized intramedullary nail for bone transport without external fixation
articles.take_home: A new internal motorized nail can regrow bone in defects and correct limb length differences without needing external fixation devices. This all-internal approach represents a new option for complex bone reconstruction.

articles.title: Antibiotic-Impregnated Bone Grafts in the Masquelet Technique Reduce the Risk of Persistent Infection at Early Follow-up.
articles.authors: Fonkoue L, Wembou S, Muluem K, Mayopa C, Bombah F, Ngongang O, et al.
articles.study_type: Retrospective study of prospectively collected data
articles.population: Adult patients with infected segmental bone defects treated with the induced membrane technique (Masquelet technique)
articles.sample_size: 40 patients (13 in antibiotic-impregnated bone graft group, 27 in standard autologous bone graft group)
articles.outcomes: Bone union and infection recurrence at mean follow-up of 20.7 months
articles.take_home: Antibiotic-impregnated bone grafts reduced infection recurrence from 30% to 8% overall, and in patients with persistent infection at the time of grafting, they prevented infection recurrence entirely (0% versus 75%) whilst achieving better bone healing without complications.

articles.title: Outcomes of early vs delayed medial malleolar fixation in the treatment of open ankle fractures.
articles.authors: Hughes IX, Baka DR, Wright BJ, Dibato JE, Gentile PM, Hwang R, et al.
articles.population: Patients with open ankle fractures involving the medial malleolus treated at a single academic trauma centre
articles.outcomes: Infection rate, length of hospital stay, number of operations, return to operating room, union rates, time to weight bearing, pain scores
articles.take_home: Early fixation of open ankle fractures reduced hospital stay and number of operations but was associated with a higher infection rate, particularly in more complex fractures. Surgeons should consider the injury severity when deciding whether to fix these fractures early or delay treatment.

articles.title: The Management of Pelvic and Vertebral Fragility Fractures: An Unmet Care Need.
articles.authors: Anderson PA, Giangregorio LM, Routt MLC Jr
articles.population: Patients with pelvic and vertebral compression fractures
articles.outcomes: Diagnosis, management approaches, and prevention of further fractures
articles.take_home: Pelvic and vertebral fractures are common but often missed because patients may have no symptoms or symptoms blamed on other conditions. Most patients improve with non-surgical treatment focusing on pain relief, mobility and nutrition, though surgery may be needed if pain is severe or the patient cannot function.

articles.title: Classification of Forearm Involvement in Multiple Hereditary Exostoses: Consensus from the CoULD Study Group.
articles.authors: Vuillermin C, Canizares MF, Miller PE, Wall LB, Steinman SE, Van Heest A
articles.study_type: Classification development and validation study using Delphi consensus method
articles.population: Children and young people with multiple hereditary exostoses affecting the forearm
articles.sample_size: 67 patients (101 radiographs for reliability testing); 15 paediatric hand surgeons in Delphi process; 4 independent surgeons for validation
articles.outcomes: Development of a new 3-tier classification system (Type 1 mild, Type 2 moderate, Type 3 severe) with improved reliability (kappa = 0.64) compared to existing classifications
articles.take_home: Experts have created a new, more reliable classification system for assessing forearm deformities in multiple hereditary exostoses. This system should help doctors monitor patients more consistently over time.

articles.title: Revision Risk Following Primary Anatomic and Reverse TSA with an Exactech Equinoxe Compared with Other Devices: A U.S.-Based Cohort Study.
articles.authors: Prentice HA, Chang RN, Yian E, Navarro RA, Singh A, Chan DP, et al.
articles.population: Adult patients who had primary shoulder replacement surgery (anatomic or reverse) between 2005 and 2023
articles.sample_size: 13,901 patients: 8,707 anatomic replacements, 4,374 elective reverse replacements, 820 reverse replacements for fracture
articles.outcomes: Risk of needing revision (repeat) surgery within the follow-up period
articles.take_home: Patients who received Exactech Equinoxe devices for anatomic shoulder replacement had a higher risk of needing revision surgery compared to other devices, but this difference was not seen in reverse shoulder replacements. The findings are relevant given the 2024 recall of some Equinoxe devices due to packaging problems.

articles.title: Bridging the Global Implementation Gap in Immediate Weight-Bearing After Hip Fracture Surgery: The WAIT-Free Consensus for Low-Adoption Regions.
articles.authors: Mao W, Jiang J, Shi ZM, Hong CC, Turabi RY, Karim MA, et al.
articles.population: Older adults with hip fracture in low-adoption regions (China, South Asia, Southeast Asia, Middle East, Latin America, Africa)
articles.outcomes: 13 recommendations across 4 domains: shared decision-making, mobility-based stratification, fall prevention and perioperative optimisation, and postoperative stability-related triage
articles.take_home: International experts have agreed on a practical framework to help hospitals in lower-resourced regions safely implement immediate weight-bearing after hip fracture surgery, with recommendations tailored to local circumstances and capacity.

articles.title: Cooler by cooler - Forecasting transfusion demand and volumes in trauma.
articles.authors: Stolarski AE, Brady KJ, Stallings JD, Scantling D, Torres C, Ong C, et al.
articles.study_type: Retrospective cohort study using predictive algorithm development
articles.population: Trauma patients aged 18-60 years with blunt, penetrating or burn injuries
articles.outcomes: Accuracy of Field Artificial Intelligence Triage (FAIT) tool in predicting blood transfusion requirements (no transfusion, transfusion, massive transfusion, ultra-massive transfusion) and patient survival
articles.take_home: A new predictive tool using early vital signs and injury information can accurately forecast whether trauma patients will need blood transfusions and how much they will need. The tool performed well even when using only pre-hospital information, potentially helping emergency teams prepare blood supplies in advance.

articles.title: Anatomical fit of a precontoured suprapectineal plate in japanese patients with acetabular fractures: A three-dimensional morphometric study.
articles.authors: Yoshida M, Iwata M, Takahashi N
articles.study_type: Retrospective morphometric study using three-dimensional pelvic models
articles.population: Japanese patients with acetabular fractures
articles.sample_size: 12 patients (9 men, 3 women; mean age 73.5 years)
articles.outcomes: Plate fit assessed by gap measurement (poor fit defined as >5 mm), anterior overhang of plate, iliopectineal line length, pelvic curvature, correlation with anthropometric parameters
articles.take_home: A standard precontoured suprapectineal plate fitted poorly in two-thirds of Japanese patients with acetabular fractures, often because the anterior part of the plate overhung the pubic symphysis. Using patient-specific three-dimensional models before surgery may help select the right implant and plan the operation better.

articles.title: Should we remove flexible intramedullary nails after diaphyseal forearm pediatric fracture? A cohort study of 288 patients.
articles.authors: Tirta M, Eikrem-Holsaeter A, Holt EB, Olsson R, Jakobsen RB, Randsborg PH
articles.population: Children treated with elastic stable intramedullary nails for forearm fractures
articles.sample_size: 288 patients (136 underwent implant removal, 152 retained implants)
articles.outcomes: Refracture rates, early refracture (before 12 months), complications, healthcare resource use (outpatient visits and radiographic examinations)
articles.take_home: Keeping the flexible nails in place after forearm fractures in children appeared safe and did not clearly increase the risk of the bone breaking again compared with removing them, whilst reducing hospital visits and scans. However, the study was not large enough to rule out moderate differences in refracture risk between the two approaches.

articles.title: Non-union rates and complications after elective interphalangeal joint arthrodesis of the hand: a cohort study of 366 arthrodeses in 289 patients.
articles.authors: Lindberg K, Sand-Uhlen H, Clementson M, Tagil M, Raina DB, Brogren E
articles.population: Patients undergoing elective interphalangeal joint arthrodesis of the hand
articles.outcomes: Non-union rate, risk factors for non-union, frequency and distribution of complications across fixation methods
articles.take_home: The procedure had a non-union rate of 5.5% with few major complications, but hardware-related problems were common and often required removal. Men had higher odds of non-union than women, although this difference was not statistically significant.

articles.title: Medial clavicle resection for acute traumatic posterior sternoclavicular dislocation: Experience from Grenoble Alpes University Hospital.
articles.authors: Datry V, Gagnepain E, Guillot M, Pirvu A, Frey G
articles.population: Patients with acute traumatic posterior sternoclavicular dislocation treated with emergency medial clavicle resection
articles.sample_size: 25 patients (23 male, 2 female; mean age 29 years)
articles.outcomes: Primary: QuickDASH score at 12 months. Secondary: QuickDASH score at 1 month, postoperative complications, return-to-work and return-to-sport rates
articles.take_home: Emergency removal of the medial end of the collarbone for posterior sternoclavicular dislocation resulted in excellent shoulder function at 12 months, with 75% of patients having minimal disability and all patients returning to work and sport. Only minor wound infections occurred, with no serious complications.

articles.title: Operative versus nonoperative management of pelvic ring fractures in older adults: A propensity-matched analysis of mortality and complications.
articles.authors: Johnson M, Sabat L, Allam J, Perdue P, Zuelzer D
articles.study_type: Retrospective cohort study with propensity matching
articles.population: Adults aged 55 years or older with pelvic ring fractures
articles.sample_size: 5314 patients in each cohort (operative and nonoperative) after matching
articles.outcomes: Primary: 30-day and 1-year all-cause mortality. Secondary: 90-day and 2-year mortality, blood clots, pneumonia, and heart attacks at various time points
articles.take_home: Operative treatment was associated with lower mortality at 2 years but this benefit did not remain significant after accounting for patient differences. Surgery was linked to higher rates of blood clots and pneumonia, so the decision to operate should weigh improved mobility against these surgical risks.

articles.title: Determinants of road traffic injury preventive behaviors among old pedestrians: An application of the PRECEDE model.
articles.authors: Bashirian S, Ayubi E, Nezafati A, Razi T, Hosseinalipour SA, Karami S, et al.
articles.population: Adults aged 60 years or older attending comprehensive health centres in Hamadan, Iran
articles.outcomes: Factors influencing road traffic injury preventive behaviours in older pedestrians, including environmental factors, reinforcing factors, education level, marital status, hearing aid use, and insurance coverage
articles.take_home: Environmental improvements and reinforcing factors like encouragement and support are important in helping older pedestrians adopt safer road safety behaviours. Public health programmes should tailor safety advice to older people's specific needs, including accounting for hearing problems and other sensory changes.

articles.title: Structures to improve the implementation of mental health practices in adult trauma centers: A Canadian nationwide practice survey.
articles.authors: Berube M, Macedo T, O'Donnell M, Laberge-Sevigny M, Moore L, Stelfox HT, et al.
articles.population: Trauma program leaders at Canadian trauma centers
articles.outcomes: Implementation of mental health structures including referral mechanisms, screening protocols, and follow-up programmes
articles.take_home: Most Canadian trauma centers have some mental health structures in place, such as screening for suicidal thoughts and substance use, but there is room for improvement in implementing evidence-based mental health practices across all trauma centres.

articles.title: Trends, disparities, and forecasts of osteosarcoma mortality in the United States, 1999-2035.
articles.authors: Gu Y, Wang T, Liu B
articles.study_type: Epidemiological analysis of mortality trends and forecasting study
articles.population: People aged 15 years and over in the United States
articles.sample_size: All osteosarcoma deaths recorded in CDC WONDER database from 1999-2023
articles.outcomes: Age-adjusted mortality rates per 100,000 population; temporal trends in mortality by sex, age group, race and ethnicity, region, and urban-rural classification; projected mortality rates to 2035
articles.take_home: Osteosarcoma deaths in the USA have increased slightly over 25 years, with higher rates in men, older adults, Non-Hispanic White people, the South, and non-metropolitan areas. Rates are expected to continue rising through 2035.

articles.title: Disparities in traumatic brain injury-related deaths - United States, 2023.
articles.authors: Waltzman D, Daugherty JD, Thomas KE
articles.study_type: Surveillance study analysing national mortality data
articles.population: All deaths with traumatic brain injury in the United States in 2023
articles.outcomes: TBI-related death rates by age, sex, race/ethnicity, injury cause, and geography; leading causes of TBI death identified
articles.take_home: In 2023, over 68,000 people died from traumatic brain injury in the US, with suicide and falls being the leading causes. Older adults aged 75 and over, males, and American Indian/Alaska Native individuals had the highest death rates and would benefit most from targeted prevention efforts.

articles.title: Understanding the outliers: A qualitative analysis of leaders' perspectives on performance and safety in trauma centers.
articles.authors: Hamad DM, Conn LG, Haas B, Jerath A, Nathens AB
articles.population: Leaders at trauma centres (Chief Safety Officers, Directors of Quality and Safety, Trauma Medical Directors, Trauma Program Managers)
articles.sample_size: 28 participants across 15 trauma centres (8 high-performing, 7 low-performing)
articles.outcomes: Themes related to safety culture, high-reliability organisation principles, communication and relationship-building
articles.take_home: Leaders at the best-performing trauma centres were more likely to use high-reliability organisation principles and focus on preventing failures and building strong workplace relationships. Low-performing centres less frequently used these approaches, suggesting that adopting these safety principles may help improve trauma centre performance.

articles.title: Epidemiology of hand fractures in children - A population-based study with data from the Danish National Patient Registry.
articles.authors: Raja A, Faergemann C, Gundtoft P, Viberg B
articles.population: Children aged 0-15 years in Denmark
articles.outcomes: Incidence of hand fractures (748 per 100,000 children per year), anatomical distribution, and treatment type. Boys accounted for 59% of cases. Highest incidence in 12-15 year age group (51%). Finger fractures most common (60%), followed by metacarpal fractures (19%). Only 1% received surgical treatment.
articles.take_home: Hand fractures in children are common and have increased by 17% over the past 20 years, with older boys (aged 12-15) most affected. Most fractures are to the fingers and heal without surgery.

articles.title: Hemorrhage control in hemodynamically unstable pelvic fractures using external fixation, angioembolization, or combined treatment: Outcomes from a level 1 trauma center.
articles.authors: De Bondt S, Kaur A, Gilleir M, Metsemakers WJ, Hoekstra H, Misselyn D, et al.
articles.population: Patients with hemodynamically unstable pelvic fractures at a level 1 trauma centre
articles.sample_size: 79 patients out of 2921 presenting with pelvic fractures
articles.outcomes: 1-year mortality rate, time to embolisation, blood transfusion requirements, treatment-related characteristics
articles.take_home: One in five patients with unstable pelvic fractures died within a year, with traumatic brain injury being the main cause rather than differences between treatment approaches. Doing external fixation first did not delay the angioembolisation procedure for patients who needed both treatments.

articles.title: Anterior fix-and-replace strategy using direct anterior and pararectus approaches for acetabular fractures in older patients.
articles.authors: Ivanova S, Keel F, Keel MJ, Siebenrock KA, Tannast M, Bastian JD
articles.population: Patients aged 60 years or older with acetabular fractures suitable for fix-and-replace strategy
articles.outcomes: Revision surgery within two years, surgical time, blood loss, 30-day complications, mortality, weight bearing, pain, mobility, and patient satisfaction
articles.take_home: Four patients (20%) needed revision surgery within two years, mainly for infection or instability. Most surviving patients were able to walk and had good pain relief and satisfaction with the treatment.

articles.title: Persistent postoperative hypercoagulability and venous thromboembolism risk following pelvic and acetabular fractures: A prospective pilot study.
articles.authors: Clarke A, Tera Y, Skeith L, Othman M, Dodd A, Duffy P, et al.
articles.population: Adults undergoing surgical treatment of pelvic and acetabular fractures
articles.outcomes: Postoperative hypercoagulability measured by thromboelastography (TEG) at multiple time points up to 3 months; venous thromboembolism (VTE) development detected by compression ultrasound and clinical assessment
articles.take_home: Despite standard blood clot prevention treatment lasting 28 days, most patients with pelvic and acetabular fractures showed signs of abnormal blood clotting that persisted for weeks or months after surgery, and nearly one in four patients developed blood clots. Current treatment duration may not be long enough for these high-risk fractures.

articles.title: Epidemiology of sports- and recreation-related shoulder and elbow injuries in older adults presenting to emergency departments in the United States between 2010 and 2024.
articles.authors: Adio AA, Boufadel P, Ilyas MH, Black EM, Hill BW, Kassam HF, et al.
articles.study_type: Epidemiological analysis using national surveillance data
articles.population: Adults aged 65 years and older presenting to emergency departments with sports- or recreation-related shoulder or elbow injuries
articles.outcomes: Injury demographics, diagnoses, seasonality, injury mechanisms, and trends from 2010 to 2024
articles.take_home: Sports-related shoulder and elbow injuries in older adults are increasing, with bicycling being the most common cause and fractures making up a substantial portion of injuries. These injuries peaked during summer months.

articles.title: CT-based three-dimensional fracture mapping reveals characteristic patterns in pelvic insufficiency fractures.
articles.authors: Jackle K, Radke Y, Lehmann N, Meier MP, Hawellek T, Roch PJ, et al.
articles.study_type: Retrospective observational study with three-dimensional imaging analysis
articles.population: Older adults with pelvic insufficiency fractures
articles.outcomes: Location and distribution of 184 fracture lines mapped using CT-based three-dimensional heatmaps; sacral alae accounted for 54% of fractures, parasymphyseal region 22%, anterior pelvic ring 15%, iliac wing 6%, acetabulum 3%
articles.take_home: In older people with pelvic fractures from osteoporosis, the sacral alae (back part of the pelvis) is the most common fracture location. The study created detailed three-dimensional maps showing how fracture patterns become more widespread in more severe types of pelvic fractures.

articles.title: Reverse-engineering the diagnostic process: An indirect finding-driven deep learning model for pelvic active bleeding detection on CT that achieves specialist-level performance and surpasses residents - a multicenter study.
articles.authors: Okada N, Inoue S, Hirano Y, Liu C, Mitarai S, Honda S, et al.
articles.study_type: Multicenter diagnostic accuracy study with deep learning algorithm development
articles.population: Patients with blunt trauma and pelvic injuries
articles.outcomes: Detection of active pelvic bleeding on contrast-enhanced CT; algorithm accuracy compared to residents and specialists; inference time
articles.take_home: A deep learning system for detecting active bleeding in pelvic trauma on CT scans achieved accuracy comparable to specialist radiologists and outperformed trainee doctors, whilst providing results in under 2 seconds. This tool could help speed up diagnosis and guide urgent treatment in seriously injured patients.

articles.title: Using injury prevention priority scores to investigate adult traumatic injuries in Nova Scotia, Canada.
articles.authors: Green D, Jessula S, Opra I, Green RS
articles.population: Adults aged 20 years and older with major traumatic injuries in Nova Scotia, Canada
articles.outcomes: Injury Prevention Priority Scores (IPPS) calculated for injury mechanisms using frequency combined with injury severity, mortality, resource utilization, and societal cost
articles.take_home: Falls and motor vehicle collisions are the leading causes of serious injury in Nova Scotia that could benefit most from prevention efforts. Falls cause the most severe injuries and hospital costs, whilst motor vehicle collisions have the highest societal costs, and both falls and intentional self-harm have high mortality rates.

articles.title: Therapeutic potential of dermal matrix in orthopaedic trauma.
articles.authors: Christenson MM, Boike SC, Puckett HD, Agoro KS, Sullivan D, Vang S, et al.
articles.population: Orthopaedic trauma patients with non-closable traumatic, infectious, or post-surgical wounds
articles.outcomes: Wound healing without skin graft, requirement for additional skin grafting or plastic surgery, time to healing, complication rates
articles.take_home: Dermal matrix helped 56% of wounds heal without needing a skin graft, and was a reliable treatment option for complex orthopaedic wounds including those with exposed bone or hardware. The treatment did not require specialist plastic surgery training.

articles.title: State-level retrospective analysis of the burden of emergency and operative conditions in India from 1980 to 2023.
articles.authors: Gerardo R, Zadey S, Shetty R, Arora A, Gupta U, Rao S, et al.
articles.study_type: State-level retrospective analysis of disease burden data
articles.population: 31 Indian states and Union Territories
articles.outcomes: Mortality rates and disability-adjusted life-years (DALYs) for emergency, operative, and emergency-operative conditions from 1980 to 2023
articles.take_home: In 2023, emergency and operative conditions accounted for nearly half of all deaths and 40% of disability burden in India, though rates have generally improved over the past four decades. Some states like Telangana, Chhattisgarh and Uttarakhand continue to have higher burdens from these conditions, indicating that surgical care needs to be a higher priority in healthcare planning across India.

articles.title: Clinical practice guidelines for moderate to severe paediatric traumatic brain injury in Australasia: A scoping review.
articles.authors: He W, Dravid A, John-Denny B, Soundappan SS
articles.study_type: Scoping review of clinical practice guidelines
articles.population: Children with moderate to severe traumatic brain injury in Australia and New Zealand
articles.sample_size: Nine guidelines included from 866 screened articles
articles.outcomes: Quality appraisal of guidelines using AGREE-II tool; identification of key management themes in acute care
articles.take_home: The PREDICT guideline was the only high-quality guideline for managing moderate to severe paediatric traumatic brain injury in Australasia. Most hospital-based guidelines lacked transparent development methods and rigorous methodology, though they were often practical to use.
